newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria favours June privatisation by govt.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria favours June privatisation by govt.

text.p: Bank Austria said on Monday it hoped the government would time the placement of its 19 percent Bank Austria stake to coincide with a three billion schillings capital increase by the bank in June.

"Bank Austria will support the republic in the privatisation of its Bank Austria shares through a wide placement. It would make sense to carry out the placement at the same time as the planned capital increase," chief executive Gerhard Randa told a news conference.
The Austrian government has said it will sell its Bank Austria stake some time this year.
Earlier, Bank Austria said it would issue preference shares worth three billion schillings at market value in June. Salomon Brothers will act as lead manager in the global offering.
On Monday, preferred shares in Bank Austria were trading 3.05 schillings down at 406.95. That would mean issuing around 7.4 million shares with a total nominal value of 740 million schillings.
"Bank Austria sees the capital increase as an important step to strengthening the involvement of private investors," the bank said in a statement. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
